snippet.title: There Isn't a Single 3D Model in This Space Game  |   Devlog
snippet.description:
Believe it or not, there isn't a single 3D model in Wingmen Chronicles. Not while you play.

Here's how every ship in our space combat sim becomes pixel art, and how flat pictures fly like real 3D craft.

How it works:

  • Concept art first: silhouettes, colours, insignia
  and four clean views for every ship.
  • The bake: a virtual studio photographs each ship
  from 802 directions and measures the depth of every
  pixel.
  • Pixel art: every picture becomes a sprite with the
  ship's own 256-colour palette.
  • Detail levels: from 48 pixels far away to 384 pixels
  up close, morphing smoothly between the steps.
  • In flight, every frame blends the three nearest
  pictures into the exact angle, so ships turn freely.
  • Light on top: engine glow, position lamps, shield
  flashes, and a cockpit that lights up with every hit.

  0:00 Not a single 3D model
  0:16 The bake: 802 views per ship
  0:30 From 48 to 384 pixels
  0:44 Light, and one sky full of ships

  Wingmen Chronicles is a space combat sim in the spirit
  of the 90s cockpit classics: fly with your wingman,
  dogfight raider aces, take on capital ships and live
  aboard the carrier TCS Resolute.

  🔔 Subscribe for more behind the scenes and cockpit
  gameplay.
  💬 Would you have guessed these were flat pictures?

  #gamedev #pixelart #indiegame
